title: Case System vNext task-specific strategy profiles
description: Pilot task-specific strategy profiles layered over shared base rules and anchored to the audit-seeded 23-domain taxonomy. Physics, Chemistry, Biology, Computer Science, Mathematics, Writing/Rhetoric, and History profiles are task-scoped; broad domain membership never defines the final strategy.

profiles.strategyScope: Solving and generalizing conjugate-product structure for a learner who already knows distributive reasoning and basic symbolic manipulation.

criteria.label: Correctness
criteria.description: The reasoning and result are mathematically valid.

criteria.label: Human reasoning efficiency
criteria.description: The visible route avoids unnecessary mechanical work when an accessible structural route exists.

criteria.label: Reasoning transparency
criteria.description: The key structural move is justified at the learner's prerequisite level.

criteria.label: Generalization quality
criteria.description: When the teaching target calls for it, the response exposes and justifies the reusable identity.

constraints: Do not reward hidden model search, token brevity, or unexplained theorem invocation.
nonGoals: No claim that the shortest symbolic derivation is always pedagogically best.

profiles.strategyScope: Deriving a reusable pair-sum solution under an authored prerequisite set that includes hash maps/sets and Big-O basics.

criteria.label: Correctness
criteria.description: The algorithm solves the stated problem under the given constraints.

criteria.label: Complexity fit
criteria.description: The method avoids unnecessary pair enumeration when the allowed data structures support a better asymptotic route.

criteria.label: Insight transparency
criteria.description: The response explains why complement lookup removes one search dimension.

criteria.label: Prerequisite fit
criteria.description: The method stays inside the learner's known concepts and allowed methods.

constraints: Do not prefer a more advanced structure merely because it is more sophisticated.
nonGoals: No transfer of this profile to debugging, refactoring, systems design, or testing.

profiles.strategyScope: Synthesizing partially conflicting sources into an original argument while preserving evidence boundaries and uncertainty.

criteria.label: Claim coherence
criteria.description: The organizing claim or tension remains logically coherent.

criteria.label: Source integration
criteria.description: Sources are related to one another rather than serially summarized.

criteria.label: Evidence fidelity
criteria.description: The response does not overstate what sources support.

criteria.label: Uncertainty preservation
criteria.description: Real disagreement or limitation is retained rather than flattened into false consensus.

constraints: Different valid organizing structures may be equally acceptable.
nonGoals: No preference for claim-centered over tension-centered synthesis absent an authored task constraint.

profiles.strategyScope: Weighing conflicting historical or social-science sources using provenance, claims, and independent corroboration.

criteria.label: Provenance reasoning
criteria.description: Source origin, incentives, and context are used as evidence rather than as automatic authority.

criteria.label: Corroboration
criteria.description: Claims are checked against independent evidence or cross-source consistency.

criteria.label: Evidentiary weight
criteria.description: Conflicting sources are not treated as equally strong merely because they disagree.

criteria.label: Bounded conclusion
criteria.description: The conclusion matches the available evidence and leaves unresolved uncertainty explicit.

constraints: Primary-source status is not sufficient for preference.
Do not collapse disagreement into false equivalence.
nonGoals: No claim that one source type is categorically superior.

profiles.strategyScope: Interpreting a position-time graph by separating directly observable kinematic relationships from unsupported causal or force claims.

criteria.label: Representation fidelity
criteria.description: Claims follow from the actual axes, scale, interval, and graphical structure rather than from an imagined physical story.

criteria.label: Kinematic validity
criteria.description: The response correctly distinguishes position, displacement, slope-related motion information, and what is not directly encoded.

criteria.label: Scope control
criteria.description: The response does not infer force, intent, or mechanism from a position-time graph without additional evidence.

criteria.label: Unit and interval awareness
criteria.description: The response attends to units and the exact interval being interpreted.

constraints: Use only graph-supported kinematic claims unless additional physical evidence is explicitly supplied.
Do not reward a causal explanation for sounding physically plausible if the graph does not identify the cause.
nonGoals: No transfer of this profile to force diagrams, energy reasoning, circuits, thermodynamics, or experimental design.

profiles.strategyScope: Designing a kinetics experiment that separates temperature and concentration effects while preserving chemical control conditions and measurement interpretability.

criteria.label: Factor identifiability
criteria.description: The design allows temperature and concentration effects to be distinguished rather than changing them in an uninterpretable bundle.

criteria.label: Chemical control
criteria.description: Other reaction conditions that materially affect rate are held fixed or explicitly accounted for.

criteria.label: Rate measurement validity
criteria.description: The proposed observable genuinely supports reaction-rate comparison and acknowledges measurement uncertainty.

criteria.label: Replication and information value
criteria.description: Replicates or additional conditions add discriminating evidence rather than procedural volume.

criteria.label: Mechanism restraint
criteria.description: The response does not claim a detailed kinetic mechanism from evidence that only supports a rate-factor relationship.

constraints: Temperature and concentration must not be varied together unless the design can separately identify their contributions.
A single noisy observation is insufficient for a confident kinetic conclusion.
nonGoals: No transfer of this profile to stoichiometry, equilibrium, spectroscopy, or organic reaction mechanisms.

profiles.strategyScope: Repairing a biological causal explanation by connecting observations to a plausible mechanism while controlling alternative biological and environmental explanations.

criteria.label: Mechanism-evidence link
criteria.description: A proposed biological mechanism is tied to observations instead of being asserted from correlation alone.

criteria.label: Control awareness
criteria.description: Relevant biological or environmental controls are identified when they could explain the observed result.

criteria.label: Alternative hypotheses
criteria.description: Competing explanations are preserved when the current evidence does not discriminate among them.

criteria.label: Biological level consistency
criteria.description: The explanation does not jump between organismal, cellular, molecular, or ecological levels without a justified bridge.

criteria.label: Teleology restraint
criteria.description: Purpose-language is not substituted for a causal biological mechanism.

constraints: Correlation may motivate a mechanism hypothesis but cannot by itself establish that mechanism.
Biological variation and uncontrolled environmental factors must remain visible when material.
nonGoals: No transfer of this profile to genetics probability, taxonomy, physiology calculation, or evolutionary inference.

profiles.strategyScope: Debugging a deterministic Python mutable-state defect by localizing the first violated invariant and proposing the smallest evidence-backed repair.

criteria.label: Fault localization
criteria.description: The response identifies the earliest state transition that makes the observed execution diverge from the intended invariant.

criteria.label: Python semantics
criteria.description: The diagnosis respects Python list/dict mutation, aliasing, evaluation order, and function-call behavior relevant to the case.

criteria.label: Evidence-backed diagnosis
criteria.description: The proposed cause is supported by a trace, targeted test, or invariant check rather than by speculative rewriting.

criteria.label: Patch minimality
criteria.description: The repair changes only what is needed to restore the intended invariant unless broader refactoring is part of the task.

criteria.label: Regression awareness
criteria.description: The response checks or names the behavior that should remain unchanged after the repair.

constraints: Use Python semantics actually present in the authored case.
Do not reward a wholesale rewrite when the fault can be localized and minimally repaired.
nonGoals: No universal Computer Science debugging strategy ranking.
No transfer of this profile to Java object models, Rust ownership, asynchronous systems debugging, or algorithm-design complexity.
